# Purchases

> Generated from the code by `scripts/generate-docs-reference.ts`. Do not edit this file: change the code and run `npm run docs:reference`.

What purchase sessions decide, and the numbers they run on. The guide is [Selling on iPhone, Android and the web](../../guides/purchases.md); the shapes are in [Models](./models.md).

## Where a purchase may go

Read from the policy code with an App Store, a Google Play and a gateway provider configured. The platform policy is [PlatformPolicy](models.md#platformpolicy).

| Platform | Policy | Store | Gateway |
|---|---|---|---|
| ios | `store` | Apple App Store (`app_store`) | never |
| android | `store` | Google Play (`google_play`) | never |
| android | `user_choice` | Google Play (`google_play`) | only after the customer picks the alternative |
| android | `gateways` | none | the best gateway, chosen by the router |
| web | `gateways` | none | the best gateway, chosen by the router |
| any platform, physical goods | not applicable | none | the best gateway, chosen by the router |

## Statuses

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `SessionStatus.Open` | `open` | Created. The customer has not come back from the checkout yet. |
| `SessionStatus.AwaitingPayment` | `awaiting_payment` | The customer has paid or approved but the provider has not confirmed yet (a mandate pending at the bank), or the customer chose the alternative payment on Google's screen and the gateway checkout is under way. A confirmation (`complete` or a webhook event) finishes it. |
| `SessionStatus.Completed` | `completed` | Paid or authorised and recorded as an entitlement. |
| `SessionStatus.Failed` | `failed` | A verification said the purchase was not paid or not authorised. Not final: a later result or event that shows the money moved (a customer who retries on the same Cashfree order) completes the session. |
| `SessionStatus.Expired` | `expired` | `expiresAt` passed without a payment. Not final either: a payment confirmed afterwards still completes it. |

| Status | Gives access | Blocks a second purchase | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `active` | yes | yes | Paid and current. A paid one-time purchase stays `active`. |
| `trialing` | yes | yes | In a free trial. |
| `past_due` | yes | yes | A charge failed and is being retried; the subscription is alive. |
| `paused` | no | yes | Charging is paused. |
| `halted` | no | no | Retries are exhausted; no further automatic charges. |
| `cancelled` | no | no | Ended. Terminal. |
| `expired` | no | no | The term ended (expired, or every cycle was collected). Terminal. |
| `refunded` | no | no | A one-time purchase that was refunded in full. Terminal. |

## When a gateway fails to create the purchase

The next ranked gateway is tried when the create call of a gateway fails with `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `NETWORK`, `TIMEOUT`, `AUTH`, `PROVIDER_ERROR`, `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`. Of the codes in that list, `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `NETWORK`, `TIMEOUT`, `AUTH`, `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` count as the gateway being unavailable and feed its circuit breaker. A refusal of the purchase's inputs (`VALIDATION` or `UNSUPPORTED`) also moves on to the next gateway, because nothing was created, and is recorded as a failed request, never as the gateway being unavailable. `CONFLICT` stops at once. See [Selling on iPhone, Android and the web](../../guides/purchases.md#when-a-gateway-fails).

## Reports to Google

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ReportKind.Transaction` | `transaction` | A first purchase, a free trial, or a renewal: `createexternaltransaction`. |
| `ReportKind.Refund` | `refund` | A refund: `refundexternaltransaction`. |

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ReportStatus.Queued` | `queued` | Waiting to be sent (or to be sent again). |
| `ReportStatus.Sent` | `sent` | Google accepted it. Final. |
| `ReportStatus.Rejected` | `rejected` | Google refused it as invalid (`VALIDATION`). Never retried: fix the data and enqueue it again by hand. |

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `FlushOutcome.Sent` | `sent` |  |
| `FlushOutcome.Retrying` | `retrying` | The attempt failed; the report stays queued and is tried again after a backoff. |
| `FlushOutcome.Blocked` | `blocked` | Waiting for the report it refers to (the first transaction of a renewal, the transaction of a refund). |
| `FlushOutcome.Rejected` | `rejected` | Google refused it as invalid; it will not be retried. |
| `FlushOutcome.NoReporter` | `no_reporter` | No reporter is configured, so nothing can be sent. The report stays queued. |

## Problems the purchase configuration reports

A bad catalog or policy throws `CONFIG` listing every problem at once. The problems it names:

| Problem | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `duplicate_product_key` | Two products share a key. |
| `subscription_without_interval` | A subscription has no interval. |
| `one_time_with_interval` | A one-time product has an interval. |
| `one_time_with_trial` | A one-time product has a trial. |
| `physical_goods_with_store_product` | A physical-goods product has an App Store or Google Play mapping. |
| `missing_app_store_provider` | A product is sold on iOS but the App Store provider is not configured. |
| `missing_app_store_product` | A product sold on iOS has no `appStore` mapping. |
| `missing_google_play_provider` | A product is sold through Google Play but the Google Play provider is not configured. |
| `missing_google_play_product` | A product sold through Google Play has no `googlePlay` mapping. |
| `missing_gateway` | A platform sells through the gateways (or through the alternative of user choice billing) and no gateway is configured. |
| `missing_tax_rate` | A product sold through user choice billing has no `taxRateBps`. |
| `missing_reporter` | The Android policy is `user_choice` and the Google Play provider that reports to Google is not configured. |
| `missing_customer_state` | A start under user choice billing had no `customer.state`. A fault of the request: `VALIDATION`. |
| `platform_not_offered` | A start named a platform the product is not sold on. A fault of the request: `VALIDATION`. |
| `provider_kind_mismatch` | The provider that owns a store mapping is of the wrong kind. |

## Problems reported to `onIssue`

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `PurchaseIssue.UnmatchedRefund` | `unmatched_refund` | A refund of a user choice billing transaction that matches no reported transaction. |
| `PurchaseIssue.ReportNotQueued` | `report_not_queued` | A user choice billing charge the library could not queue a report for. |
| `PurchaseIssue.DuplicatePurchase` | `duplicate_purchase` | A customer paid for the same product in two sessions (for example on the web and on a phone at the same time). Both entitlements are kept because the money has moved; refund or cancel one. |
| `PurchaseIssue.EventFailed` | `event_failed` | An event could not be applied; the others of its batch were. |
| `PurchaseIssue.OutcomeNotRecorded` | `outcome_not_recorded` | The router could not record an outcome (its statistics store failed). The purchase went on. |

## Numbers

| Setting | Default |
|---|---|
| Time an unpaid session stays open (`sessionTtlMs`) | 24 hours |
| Deadline Google sets for a report, from the transaction time | 24 hours |
| Reports one flush sends at most (`limit`) | 50 |
| Wait before the first retry of a failed report (`retry.baseMs`), doubled each time | 1 minute |
| Longest wait between retries (`retry.maxMs`) | 1 hour |
| Time a flush owns the reports it claimed (`reportLeaseMs`) | 5 minutes |
| Lifetime of a lock (`lock.ttlMs`) | 2 minutes |
| Time a request waits for a lock before `CONFLICT` (`lock.waitMs`) | 15 seconds |

## The purchases file of the service

`serve` reads one JSON file named by `PURCHASES_FILE`. It has these keys and no others; a misspelt key is an error.

| Key | Holds |
|---|---|
| `catalog` | The products you sell: a list of Product. At least one. |
| `policy` | Where each platform may buy: PlatformPolicy. Optional; the defaults are the App Store on iOS, Google Play on Android and the gateways on the web. |
| `routing` | The routing strategy: RoutingStrategy. Optional; the router uses its defaults. |
